notes.title: Patch #1
notes.content:
Friends! We've launched the first patch in which:
[list]
[*] Many bugs fixed (We hope - almost all of this little basterds)

[/list]

I have no excuse! ːsteamsaltyː

And have a good trip!" - [/i] Michael Rfdshir

notes.title: Ultra Strangeness
notes.content:
Hi! Hope you like Wurroom. It's my first game, and it's small, so I decide to make it a gift for all who like strange games)

And now I'm working on a bigger exploration adventure game that will be released in 2020.
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/986520/Ultra_Strangeness]Ultra Strangeness on Steam[/url]

It's a game that's also made of plasticine.
Unlike the Wurroom, it has:
[list]
[*]more classic and consistent story (but, of course, with psychedelic inclusions)
[*]more detailed and diverse gameplay
[*] and even more unusual animations!
[/list]  

Just add it to the whistlist if you interested, so you never miss it!

[previewyoutube=9FM91JuhcW0;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Meet Serge Bulat
notes.content:
Hi! It seems right to tell about the people behind the project. And let's start with Serge Bulat, whose music has become a source of inspiration for the extraordinary Wurroom universe.

Serge Bulat is a Moldovan born music artist, whose eclectic sound fuses electronica, neo-classical, world & experimental styles. 

Bulat has been involved in both European & American scenes, exploring in various art mediums: from music and video to radio and theater productions. 

Bulat's artistic approach is often perceived as a meditation on arts, philosophy, science, and society; and explores such diverse subjects as creativity, technology, reality, and identity.

Artist's most notable to date works are:
[list]

[*]"Queuelbum", the concept project that won an IMA award (New York) for Best Electronic Album Of The Year. 

[*]"Third World Walker", the audio/visual installations presented at the festivals in more than 10 countries. 

[*]"Inkblot" - the multimedia piece, launched at the VU 3 - Symposium for experimental, electronic and improvised music in Park City, Utah, along with the radio appearance on CKCU FM 93.1's "Acoustic Frontiers."

[*]"Yehy Vaya" - the collaboration with Mordovian folk band OYME (Deep Forest), sung in the indigenous language of Erzya.
[/list]
